subject: SLA handshake: capacity fingerprinting and peak-to-baseline reconciliation
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@brightcart.io>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: eng@brightcart.io
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery — throughput & streaming notes

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap from BrightCart so we're aligned on the workload fingerprint and our asks: 

- Baseline (steady): ~3 QPS (user-agent driven checks and background tasks)
- Peak crest (promotions, checkout flood): short bursts up to ~40 QPS for 3-8 minute windows several times/day
- Typical response size: 600-900 tokens (avg ~750 tokens) per response for product-summary + contextual personalization
- Streaming: ~12% of sessions open a streaming connection (progressive personalization) with expected session keepalive ~45-120s
- Concurrency: we typically see 60 concurrent sessions at peak, of which ~8 are streaming concurrently
- Latency SLO target: p95 <= 350ms for non-streaming, p95 <= 600ms for streaming tail (we understand streaming has higher tail variability)

Immediate asks from us: 
1) Confirmation of how you translate tokens/sec and QPS into reserved capacity (ballpark GPUs + expected headroom).
2) Any profiling artifacts you need (sample payloads, traces, logs).
3) A lightweight pilot plan to validate p95 under peak crest with our real traffic shape.

Attached are sample payloads and a short CSV showing a 72-hour traffic extract (capacity-snapshot.csv). Happy to schedule a brief ops handoff if you need to loop in infra.

- Elena
Director, Engineering — BrightCart

-----Original Message-----
On Wed, Sep 29, 2027 at 08:03 AM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks for joining the call — notes to follow.

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: Elena Torres <elena@brightcart.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery — throughput & streaming notes

Elena — thanks for the crisp summary and for sharing the CSV. I translated the numbers from the call into a working hypothesis below: 

- Steady state: 3 QPS * 750 tok = ~2,250 tok/sec
- Peak crest: 40 QPS * 750 tok = ~30,000 tok/sec (sustained for 3-8 min bursts)
- Streaming slice: concurrent streaming sessions ~8 at peak, with incremental per-session tokens/sec dependent on chunk size (we'll need your chunking pattern)

Immediate answers to your asks: 
1) Ballpark reserved capacity: based on our internal benchmarks for the base model family you indicated, one A100-class GPU in our optimized runtime typically sustains ~40k–80k tok/sec depending on quantization and sequence length. Conservatively, to meet p95<=350ms for non-streaming with headroom for bursts, we estimate starting with 2 reserved GPUs for the initial pilot and autoscale to +1 when the crest windows are detected.

2) Profiling artifacts we need: sample request/response payloads (you attached), representative tokenization counts (per request), and a 30-minute HAR or request trace from a peak crest window if available. If you can strip PII that's fine.

3) Pilot plan (light):
- We provision 2 reserved GPUs in a dedicated pool for a 48-hour pilot.
- We run replay of a 2-hour crest window from your CSV during business hours to verify p95 and token throughput under realistic concurrency.
- Redwood will provide: per-route latency breakdown, token/sec telemetry, and an ops checklist.

Next steps: Please confirm you'd like Redwood to run the replay and that we can use the attached CSV slice. Also propose a 30-minute ops handoff on Mon/Tue so Karhtik (cc) can align on autoscale + routing policy.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior AE, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Elena Torres <elena@brightcart.io>, eng@brightcart.io
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2027 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Discovery — throughput & streaming notes

Adding some ops-level calculations so we have an internal record and a concrete ask for the pilot. Notes and conservative sizing below — this is intentionally cautious until we run a live replay: 

Assumptions from Elena's CSV and Soojin's summary:
- avg tokens/response: 750
- peak QPS crest: 40
- tokens/sec peak: 40 * 750 = 30,000 tok/sec

Redwood runtime estimates (model: open-family-7b equivalent, FP16 -> int8 quantization path available):
- Conservative throughput per A100 (mixed-length, streaming-aware): ~35k tok/sec with p95 ~250-320ms on single-request flows, assuming batching for small windows and KV cache warm.
- Latency sensitivity: streaming adds framing/flush overhead; streaming tail p95 tends to be ~1.5x the non-streaming p95 under identical load shapes.

Recommendation for pilot: 
1) Start with 2x A100 reserved (dedicated pool) with autoscale +1 during crest detection. That gives a theoretical baseline capacity ~70k tok/sec (ample headroom for 30k crest).
2) Concurrency and batching knobs: target 8-12 concurrent worker threads per GPU, batching window 5–10ms for non-streaming to keep p95 under 350ms.
3) Streaming handling: pin streaming sessions to a routing lane to avoid head-of-line blocking; keep streaming concurrency capped at 12 across pool to preserve tail latency.

Pilot telemetry outputs we'll deliver: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec per-GPU, batching metrics (avg batch size, queue wait), and a breakdown of streaming-specific tail behavior.

Ops ask for Elena: please share a 30-minute crest window (HAR/trace) and confirm a time window for us to trigger the replay. Also grant a short window to run profiling with the sample payloads you provided.

I can take point on scheduling the pilot execution with Karhtik and BrightCart ops. 

- Marissa
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Torres <elena@brightcart.io>

Thanks all — this is very helpful and aligns with our internal expectations. We approve the 48-hour pilot using the 2x A100 reserved pool and autoscale +1 during crest detection. 

Action items from BrightCart (this message):

- Permission granted for Redwood to run the replay on Fri 10/1 09:00–11:00 PST (we'll be available to monitor).
- Attached sample payloads and a quick note on chunking: we send 128-token chunks for streaming updates with a max chunk rate of ~4 chunks/sec per streaming session.

Please confirm the pilot start time and the Ops call time for Thurs 09/30 11:00 AM PST for a quick alignment (15–20m).

Looking forward — Elena
